chunks: And as for what was narrated - Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Talhah ibn Zayd from Ja'far from his father - from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no harm if the boy who has not had his first seminal emission (had not reached puberty via wet dream) gives the call to prayer and leads the prayer."

This does not contradict the first report because this report is applied to one who has not had a wet dream but is a complete, rational person who led the congregation in prayer, because seminal emission is not a condition for puberty, nor is the other [type] invalid, because puberty is considered by several things, including seminal emission; so whoever's seminal emission was delayed, he is considered by what is other than that, such as hair growth and body hair, and what follows their pattern, or the perfection of intellect, even if he is devoid of all of that. And the first report includes one who has not attained any of the conditions of puberty, and there is no contradiction between them.
And we have clarified that there is no harm if the blind man leads the prayer if there is someone there to guide him and provide further explanation.

key_terms.الْاحْتِلَامُ: Seminal emission (as a sign of puberty)
key_terms.لَمْ يَحْتَلِمْ: Has not had seminal emission (wet dream)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a boy to lead congregational prayer if he has not had his first wet dream?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction between reports by distinguishing between the general requirement of puberty and the specific sign of seminal emission, noting that *bulugh* is established through multiple indicators such as hair growth or mental maturity. This jurisprudential nuance allows a boy who has not yet experienced *ihtilam* but possesses other signs of maturity to validly lead congregational prayer, ensuring the continuity of communal worship even when the imam is blind or requires guidance.
